definition: In this historical source, a cell is the basic structural and living unit of an organized body, usually described as having a membrane and protoplasmic contents such as a nucleus and cytoplasm, though some parts may be absent. In neurology, a nerve-cell means the whole structural unit of the nervous system: the cell body together with its outgoing processes, including dendrites and the axis-cylinder process.
